claim_boundary: Controlled single-node diagnostic only; no production SLA, HA/DR, multi-node, multi-GPU, MIG, MPS, or X1 claim.

diagnostics.observation: One sequential request completed with a durable terminal effect and distinct write/readback backend PIDs.
Sixteen concurrent external requests were all rejected with durable_effect_commit_failed while the service remained fail-closed.

A cold isolated PostgreSQL reproduction produced migration lock timeouts/deadlocks; a preinitialized store then committed 16/16 effects with pool_max=8, timeout=0, and a distinct readback backend PID for every effect.

rca.connection_ownership: The write transaction exits before commit-timestamp and visibility readback. Warm concurrency proved separate backend ownership without pool starvation.
rca.defect: The cached store factory was not single-flight. Concurrent first requests constructed multiple pools and ran the same schema migration, causing PostgreSQL lock timeouts/deadlocks before terminal-effect commit.
rca.remediation: Initialize one process-wide S6B-M store under a construction lock during API lifespan startup; retain the frozen pool size and two-phase write/readback ownership.
